newsitem.title: INDIA: India parliament's upper house adjourns in uproar.
newsitem.headline: India parliament's upper house adjourns in uproar.

text.p: The upper house of the Indian parliament adjourned for a second consecutive day on Thursday after lawmakers' disagreed on whether to discuss a corruption scandal first or caste tensions in western India.

Najma Heptullah, deputy chairperson of the Rajya Sabya or upper house, adjourned the proceedings amid uprorious scenes from a divided house where different parties wanted different items of on the agenda discussed first.

The Congress party has been seeking the dismissal of the regional Hindu Shiv Sena party government in western Maharashtra state, accusing it of failing to combate insults to lower caste Hindus or Dalits.
Lawmakers of the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) wanted corruption in the eastern state of Bihar to be discussed first.
Maharashtra has been rocked by tension between Dalits, and upper-caste rivals since July 11 when a statue of socialist activist and Dalit leader B.R. Ambedkar was desecrated.
At least 12 people died when police opened fire on rioters in Maharashtra's capital city, Bombay, two weeks ago.
Initially the house had been adjourned until 2 p.m. (0830 GMT) but unruly behaviour of members forced Heptullah to adjourn the house for the day. The house was also adjourned on Wednesday.
BJP lawmakers led protests against the government of Bihar, embroiled in a $280 million corruption scandal.

Bihar's chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav, who has been indicted in the corruption scandal by federal police, says he will not resign from his post. He says he is innocent in the case, which involves alleged diversion of animal welfare funds.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's ruling coalition is severly divided over its continuing association with a breakaway faction set up by Yadav early this month.
Coalition leaders are scheduled to debate the political deadlock on Friday.
